references.text: Jacob and Laban erected a stone pillar as a witness to the covenant between them, just as Joshua used the stone as a witness to the covenant between Israel and God.
Moses set up twelve stone pillars representing the twelve tribes of Israel when the covenant was made at Sinai, similar to Joshua's use of stones as covenant witnesses.
The song of Moses was to serve as a witness against Israel if they turned away from God, just as the stone was to be a witness against the people.
The Book of the Law was placed beside the Ark of the Covenant as a witness against Israel, parallel to the function of the stone as a witness.
Joshua set up twelve stones at Gilgal as a memorial of Israel's crossing over the Jordan, illustrating Joshua's use of stones as testimony.
Jacob erected a stone pillar in Bethel after his encounter with God, reflecting the tradition of using stones as witnesses to divine encounters.
Samuel set up a stone called Ebenezer as a witness to the Lord's help, similar to Joshua's use of a stone as a witness.
Isaiah was asked to write down a testimony to be preserved for the future, parallel to the function of the stone as an enduring witness.
